**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip caching wrappers on the invalid span singleton**

When a bridged no-op or shut-down tracer returns `Span.getInvalid()`, this is the shared `PropagatedSpan` singleton, so this write attaches the application wrapper to a JVM-lifetime object. Constructing another invalid `ApplicationSpan` overwrites the same slot, which makes a context containing the first wrapper round-trip through `Bridging.toApplication` as the later wrapper; the last wrapper (and its application class loader) is also retained indefinitely. Check span-context validity before associating or consulting the holder so invalid spans continue to use the canonical invalid-span path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L24-L26](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/1e893f209393f33c3269ba54f9e1e776153b08dd/AGENTS.md#L24-L26)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

replies.body: I suspect that `Span.getInvalid()` doesn't reach here. Added `agentSpan != Span.getInvalid()` just in case

threads.body: [Javaagent] When two isolated application API classloaders read the same agent span, each rejects the other's cached wrapper in `Bridging.toApplication()` and overwrites this shared slot. Returning to the original loader then loses the original span identity even though its context is unchanged, and alternating reads repeatedly discard the cached `SpanContext`. Retain associations per application API classloader or in the bridged context, and cover an A → B → A classloader round trip.

replies.body: The intent of this PR isn't really to preserve the identity but to reduce the cost of bridging. Preserving the identity just was the easiest way to test that the application span instance is cached in the agent span. I'd expect agent span being bridged to multiple class loaders to be very uncommon. If that were to happen then `if (applicationSpan instanceof application.io.opentelemetry.api.trace.Span)` check while reading the value ensures that we ignore the cached value from another class loader and fall back to conversion.

threads.body: Could also consider something like `InstrumentedAgentSpan` so it would be easier to see what it is used for.
